title:
A Modified Space Metaphor for Visualizing Multidimensional 
Data in Virtual Reality
content:
The growth in the volume of digital data, its unstructured nature, its multidimensionality, and the need to analyze such data in dynamics impose new requirements on data visualization systems. Existing two-dimensional visualization systems are limited in their ability to simultaneously display multiple dimensions of data. To overcome this limitation, virtual reality data visualization systems are being developed that create for the user the illusion of being inside a virtual information space. The most important dimensions for the analysis of multidimensional data are the temporal and semantic dimensions, since time reflects the dynamics of data, while semantics serves as the basis for their interpretation and transformation into knowledge.
	At the same time, existing approaches to data visualization in virtual reality suffer from a significant drawback, which consists in the absence of a cognitively effective representation of the temporal and semantic dimensions of multidimensional data within a unified virtual space.
	This paper proposes a new approach to visualizing multidimensional data in virtual reality that is free from this drawback and is based on a modified space metaphor. The main tenets of this approach are as follows: data are represented as a collection of entities and relations between them; the user is placed at the center of an egocentric spherical coordinate system, where individual temporal slices of data are represented as concentric spheres and time is encoded by radial distance; images of entities are placed on the inner surfaces of these spheres; semantic proximity between entities is displayed through angular distances between the corresponding images. The paper provides a detailed description of data preparation for visualization and of the modification of the space metaphor, as well as a detailed description of the visualization process itself for temporal-semantic data.
	User interaction scenarios with the visualization demonstrate that the proposed approach supports the full cycle of analytical activity from data overview to the analysis of individual entities, their semantic changes, and their relations over time within a unified spatial structure.
